title: Why portfolios drift: the 10-year example
body_md:
Rebalancing means moving money between asset classes to bring the portfolio back to its target mix. Different assets grow at different speeds, so the mix changes on its own even if the client does nothing. Illustrative: ₹20 L at a 60/40 equity/debt target, never rebalanced, with equity at 12% and debt at 7% a year.

| Point in time | Equity | Debt | Equity share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start | ₹12.0 L | ₹8.0 L | 60% |
| After 10 years | ≈ ₹37.3 L | ≈ ₹15.7 L | ≈ 70% |

The client agreed to 60% equity, but now holds 70% without ever deciding to. A big fall would now hurt more than they signed up for.
example: ₹20 L at 60/40, equity 12%, debt 7%: after 10 years ≈ ₹37.3 L equity, ≈ ₹15.7 L debt — about 70% equity, without any decision.
